quizName: DMV Practice Test #16 40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.explanation: You can use hand signals instead of or in addition to turn signals. When your left arm is bent at the elbow and points downward, it means you plan to slow down or stop.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Always pick one part of the lane to occupy and never leave that part of the lane.
Vary your lane position as conditions warrant.
Only ride in the center of the lane so other vehicles can see you more easily.
Ride in a zigzag pattern so other drivers notice you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vary your lane position as conditions warrant.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn just your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: Look through a turn toward where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: Your lane position should not:

options.text: Avoid placing you in other drivers' blind spots.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
Provide you with an escape route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: Good lane positioning helps you see better and be seen. It keeps you out of blind spots and away from hazards. It should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if needed.

questions.question: Which of the following is a poor reason to sound your horn?

options.text: A driver in the lane next to you is too close to the vehicle ahead of them.
A parked car has a person in the driver's seat.
You want people to look at your motorcycle.
You are passing someone who is in the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: You want people to look at your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Sound your horn to warn drivers or pedestrians who may move into your path. Use it when passing a vehicle, a person in a parked car, or a pedestrian in the street. Do not use it just to get attention.

questions.question: When looking through a turn to see where you are going, you should:
questions.explanation: Look through a turn toward where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: When preparing to pass a vehicle on the left, it is important to ride on the left side of your lane because:

options.text: The right side could be slippery.
It will give you the best chance of spotting hazards in the next lane.
People don't usually expect to be passed on their left.
It will place you in the rearview mirror of the car in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It will give you the best chance of spotting hazards in the next lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left part of your lane to see better and be more visible to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: If operating a three-wheeled motorcycle or riding with a sidecar, do not ride too far to the right of your lane because:

options.text: Other drivers may not see you.
You will not be able to pass other vehicles as easily.
Other drivers may try to share your lane.
You may run off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may run off the road.
questions.explanation: A sidecar sits on the right side. Riding too far right risks the sidecar leaving the road. On a three-wheeled motorcycle, the rear right wheel may go off the road if you get too close to the right edge.

questions.question: If road conditions require a longer stopping distance than normal, you should:

options.text: Ask someone else to operate your motorcycle.

questions.explanation: When your motorcycle needs more time to stop, increase your following distance. Maintain at least three seconds of space on slippery pavement, when you cannot see ahead clearly, or in heavy traffic.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, it is recommended that you maintain a following distance of at least:
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, maintain at least two seconds of following distance. Increase this distance when conditions are not perfect.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, which of the following is NOT important?
questions.explanation: A good helmet must meet U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) standards. It should fit snugly all the way around. It should have no obvious defects like cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps. How it looks is not important for safety.

questions.question: Riding on the far side of a lane when following another vehicle:

options.text: Is recommended because drivers will see you easily.
Is not recommended because drivers rarely check their side mirrors.
Is recommended because passengers will tell the driver you are there.
Is illegal because you must ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is not recommended because drivers rarely check their side mirrors.
questions.explanation: Most drivers look at their rearview mirror more often than their side mirrors. When following a car, ride in the center of the lane. This position makes you most visible in the driver's rearview mirror.

questions.question: A child passenger should:

options.text: Sit in front of the operator.
Not be able to reach the footrests.

questions.explanation: A child should always sit directly behind the operator. A child in front may lose balance and could interfere with the operator's control of the motorcycle.

questions.question: To swerve on a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Press the handgrip toward the direction you want to go.
Press the handgrip away from the direction you want to go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip toward the direction you want to go.
questions.explanation: To swerve, press the handgrip on the side where you want to turn. To swerve left, press the left handgrip, then press the right to straighten out. To swerve right, press the right handgrip, then the left.

questions.question: Under ideal riding conditions, what is the minimum following distance?
questions.explanation: Under normal conditions, keep at least two seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance if conditions are not perfect.

questions.question: When another vehicle is passing you from behind, you should:

options.text: Use the left portion of your lane.
Use the center portion of your lane.
Use the right portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the center portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: The center of the lane is the safest position when being passed. Riding on the side closer to the passing vehicle increases crash risk. Riding on the far side might make the driver move back into your lane too soon.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to help you see.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to help you see.
questions.explanation: At night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead of you to see farther down the road. Be flexible about your lane position when riding at night.

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When you will slow down suddenly.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your signals are not working.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you will slow down suddenly.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light before slowing suddenly, especially if a vehicle is tailgating you. The tailgater may not see the hazard ahead that is making you slow down.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should do all of the following except:

options.text: Use your high beam light when possible.

questions.explanation: At night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther. Use your high beam headlight except when following or meeting another vehicle.

questions.question: Which is NOT a good way to prevent a friend from driving while intoxicated?

options.text: Arrange a safe ride home for them.
Keep them busy with other activities while they sober up.
Let them wait 15 minutes after their last drink before driving.
Get other friends to help stop them from driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let them wait 15 minutes after their last drink before driving.
questions.explanation: To prevent drinking and driving, arrange another way for them to get home, involve them in other activities to slow their drinking, use any excuse to keep them from leaving, and get friends to help stop them.

questions.question: When another vehicle passes you, which part of the lane should you ride in?
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding on the side closer to the passing vehicle increases crash risk. Riding on the far side is also dangerous because it may encourage the other driver to enter your lane too soon.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Ride more slowly than you normally would.
Start slowing earlier than you normally would.
Not communicate with the passenger while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not communicate with the passenger while riding.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight, which makes your motorcycle slower to respond. With a passenger, ride more slowly, start braking sooner, and keep more distance between you and other vehicles. Always tell your passenger about road conditions ahead.

questions.question: When making normal stops, you should:

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Alternate between the front and rear brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when slowing or stopping, even for normal stops.

questions.question: Usually, a minimum following distance of _____ should be maintained.
questions.explanation: Keep a minimum following distance of two seconds. Increase it to at least three seconds in poor riding conditions.

questions.question: On a slippery surface, you should not:

options.text: Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping.
Use both brakes when slowing or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use only the front brake when slowing or stopping.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes, reduce your speed, and avoid sudden moves. Watch for oily areas, dirt, gravel, shaded areas, and bridges—these are more likely to be slippery.

questions.question: To be effective, an eye or face shield must:

options.text: Not allow for eyeglasses to fit underneath.
Restrict your vision to the sides.

questions.explanation: An effective eye or face shield must be scratch-free, resist breaking, allow clear side vision, fasten securely, allow air to pass through to prevent fogging, and fit over eyeglasses if needed.

questions.question: If you accidentally lock your rear wheel while braking on a good traction surface, you should:

options.text: Keep it locked until you come to a complete stop.
Release the rear brake and only use the front brake.
Release the rear brake, then quickly re-apply it.
Release the rear brake and down shift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: On a good traction surface, keep the rear brake locked until you stop completely. You can still control your motorcycle if it is upright and going straight.

questions.question: When riding in a group, inexperienced riders should ride:

options.text: In the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader near the front. This lets experienced riders at the back watch over them.

questions.question: How can you regain control if your rear tire locks up?

options.text: Swerve the bike in the direction with the fewest hazards.
With the brake engaged, try to accelerate.

questions.explanation: Release the rear brake to regain control of a locked rear wheel. However, on a good traction surface, you can keep it locked until you stop completely.

questions.question: Do not change gears on railroad tracks because:

options.text: Other drivers may not be expecting you to change gears.
The uneven surface may make it more difficult to switch gears.

questions.explanation: Do not shift gears when crossing railroad tracks. Your motorcycle might stall while on the tracks.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs with white backgrounds and black letters show traffic rules. Speed limit signs are rectangular. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: If your front wheel skids while braking, you should:

options.text: Release the front brake right away and apply it smoothly again.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release both brakes and coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and apply it smoothly again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the front brake immediately. Then apply the brake smoothly again.

questions.question: In traffic, motorcycles need:

options.text: Much less distance to stop than cars.
Less distance to stop than cars.
As much distance to stop as cars.
More distance to stop than cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: As much distance to stop as cars.
questions.explanation: In traffic, a motorcycle needs the same stopping distance as a car.

questions.question: Rain suits should:

options.text: Not balloon out while you ride.
Not be needed because motorcycles should not ride in rain.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not balloon out while you ride.
questions.explanation: Good motorcycle rain suits resist tearing and ballooning when riding at high speeds.

questions.question: To carry a passenger, you may need to:
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle. You may need to adjust the shocks before carrying a passenger. You should also adjust the headlight and mirrors because the motorcycle will sit differently.

questions.question: ______ guarantees that another driver sees you.
questions.explanation: Nothing guarantees that a driver sees you. It is safest to assume that any vehicle that can enter your path will do so.

questions.question: The front brake provides how much of a motorcycle's total braking power?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 75 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: In New Hampshire, a person age 21 or older with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of ______ is considered legally intoxicated.
questions.explanation: A person of legal drinking age with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. Riding a motorcycle while intoxicated is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: If riding a three-wheel motorcycle in a group, you should travel in a:
questions.explanation: Two-wheel motorcycles can use a staggered formation. Three-wheel motorcycles are too wide for this. Groups of three-wheel motorcycles should ride in a single-file line.

questions.question: When riding with a heavy load, you should adjust the:
questions.explanation: Before riding with a heavy load, adjust your tire pressure, spring pre-load, air shocks, and dampers to match the weight you are carrying.
